content:
sasha: Heads-up — starting a canary for quant-v2-lite tonight (11:00pm PST). Need quick alignment on automatic fallback thresholds and rollback window. TL;DR: eval snippets below. Looking for agreement by 10:30pm. @maria @kevin

maria: Thanks. Can you paste the slice-level numbers and baseline so we can sanity check noise floors?

sasha: Paste from the smoke eval run: 
```
baseline: {
  mrr: 0.382,
  hallucination_rate: 0.011,  # 1.1%
  latency_p95_ms: 210
}
canary(quant-v2-lite): {
  mrr: 0.369,   # -3.4% relative
  hallucination_rate: 0.019, # 1.9% (+0.8% abs)
  latency_p95_ms: 245
}
```
Proposed hard thresholds: MRR drop >= 2.5% OR hallucination absolute increase >= 0.7% OR p95 latency > baseline + 60ms -> immediate rollback. Soft alarm: MRR drop >= 1.0% OR hallucination abs >= 0.3% -> throttle to 10% and spawn additional evals. Rollback window: immediate + re-eval after 2h.

kevin: Slight ask — make MRR rollback threshold 3.0%? worried about noisy small-sample dips causing churn.

julia: We should be slice-aware. If degradation is only in long-doc slice, hold at 5% stable traffic and run a targeted warmup + eval before rolling back cluster-wide. Long-docs and multi-turn dialogs behave differently with KV warmup.

tarun: Agreed on slice-awareness. Also suggest excluding cold-start sessions (<=2 tokens) from the canary metric to avoid noise.

devops-bot: FYI — we can express this in rollout-config and enforce via circuit-breaker. Example snippet: 
```yaml
rollout:
  canary:
    traffic_percent: 20
    window: 5m
    metrics:
      - name: mrr
        comparator: relative_decrease
        threshold: 0.025
        action: rollback
      - name: hallucination_rate
        comparator: absolute_increase
        threshold: 0.007
        action: rollback
      - name: latency_p95_ms
        comparator: absolute_increase
        threshold: 60
        action: rollback
    soft_alerts:
      - name: mrr
        comparator: relative_decrease
        threshold: 0.01
        action: throttle_to_10pct
    predicates:
      - slice_aware: ["long-doc", "multi-turn"]
      - exclude_coldstart_tokens: 2
```
Note: CI will validate config and install the circuit-breaker hook.

maria: I think hallucination threshold 0.007 (0.7%) aligns better with observed eval noise. Setting it lower than 0.005 avoids spurious tripping.

sasha: OK updating proposal: 
- Hard rollback: MRR drop >= 2.5% (relative) OR hallucination abs increase >= 0.7% OR p95 > +60ms.
- Soft alarm: MRR >= 1.0% -> throttle to 10% + extra eval set.
- Safety: three consecutive 5m windows exceeding thresholds -> immediate canary kill.
- Slice-awareness: if >80% of degradation is concentrated in a single slice (e.g., long-doc), hold promotion at 5% and run targeted KV warmup + 10k long-doc evals before global rollback.

kevin: Fine with 2.5% so long as we have the 3-window kill rule. Also add a cooldown of 30m between auto-promote attempts to avoid flip-flop.

julia: Please make sure KV warmup metric is included in telemetry (kv_hit_rate per slice). Long-doc regressions often correlate with poor kv_hit on cold hosts.

tarun: Actionable: I'll open a PR with the rollout-config + slice predicates and a small smoke job that excludes sessions with <=2 tokens. Will also add the '3-window' circuit-breaker.

maria: I'm starting an expanded eval on 10k long-doc examples (include system prompts + multi-turn). ETA ~90 minutes. I'll post results into this thread.

kevin: I'll add the alerting playbook and a runbook for manual rollback steps (who to page, metrics to check, how to pin back to baseline variant).

devops-bot: PR template created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rollouts/pull/1428 — CI lint is running. When merged, the rollout-controller will validate metrics hooks and enable canary gate.

sasha: Sounds good. If no objections by 10:30pm PST we'll proceed with the 20% canary at 11pm. Final ask: everyone OK with the updated thresholds + 3-window kill + slice-aware holdback? :eyes:

maria: OK from my side.

kevin: OK

julia: OK, but please ensure kv telemetry before cutover.

tarun: PR up in draft, ping me for review.

sasha: Great — I'll kick off unless someone raises an objection before 10:30pm. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
